items.title: 67425_Tiny Grimes oral history interview
items.q: I think Fats Domino started off, as far as the drums is concerned, with this beat they call New Orleans beat

ctx.x: But everybody way back, yeah, because see its the matter of support, you know. The kids that like rock and roll they support it. The kids, or the people that liked jazz didn't support it.

Rhythm and blues was over on a more softer volume. I think Fats Domino started off, as far as the drums is concerned, with this beat they call New Orleans beat -- or somethin' the drummer was doin' -- some kind of funny name -- somethin' like that. And the rock and rollers just enforced it more, and I stayed on -- the thing that dugged me -- this just stayed on a couple of chords -- two or three chords. And it seemed to be that the beat was the one that was carryin' everything over, not the music.
Q. Did you try to play in that kind of style at all, since it was so popular?
